notes.text: Broil the skewers in two batches, or on two sheet pans one after the other, so they sit in one layer under the broiler.

callback.body: Butter chicken sat in a yogurt and spice marinade before it cooked, and so does this. The new part is the heat: instead of a pan, the broiler cooks the chicken from above.

move.title: Soak it, then char it
move.body: Shish taouk is Lebanon's chicken on skewers. The chicken sits in a marinade of yogurt, lemon, garlic, and spices, then cooks under the broiler, the oven's top heat, until the edges char and the middle is juicy. It's wrapped in warm pita with a quick garlic yogurt sauce and crunchy vegetables.

why.title: Yogurt makes it tender
why.body: Yogurt is gently sour. It softens the outside of the chicken slowly without turning it mushy, and the milk in it helps the edges brown. That's why so many marinades from Lebanon to India start with yogurt.

why.title: Half an hour, or all day
why.body: Thirty minutes in the marinade flavors the outside of the chicken. A few hours in the fridge flavors it more deeply. Marinating chicken always happens in the fridge, never on the counter.

why.title: Heat from the top
why.body: A broiler is like an upside-down grill: the heat comes from above, close and strong. It cooks the top fast and chars the edges, so you turn the skewers halfway to cook the other side.

why.title: Leave a little space
why.body: Pieces jammed tight on a skewer steam each other and stay pale where they touch. A small gap between pieces lets the heat reach every side, so they brown all over.

why.title: Throw out the marinade
why.body: Marinade that held raw chicken has raw-chicken juices in it. Once the chicken comes out, pour what's left down the drain. Never use it as a sauce. That's why the sauce is made separately.

wrong.sign: The edges are black but the middle isn't 165°F
wrong.fix: Move the rack one level lower and keep broiling, checking every 2 minutes.
The rack was too low or the broiler wasn't hot. Move the pan up one level and broil 2 more minutes, watching closely.

wrong.sign: Wooden skewers caught fire at the ends
wrong.fix: Soak them longer next time, at least 30 minutes, and cover the bare ends with a strip of foil.

wrong.sign: The garlic sauce is too strong
wrong.fix: Stir in more yogurt, a spoonful at a time.

quiz.explain: Raw chicken stays cold while it marinates.

quiz.q: What do you do with the leftover marinade?
quiz.explain: It held raw chicken, so it's thrown out.

quiz.q: Where does a broiler's heat come from?
quiz.explain: That's why you turn the skewers halfway.

steps.text: If you're using wooden skewers, put them in a tall glass of water to soak.
In the large bowl, stir together the marinade's yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, and salt with the tomato paste, paprika, cumin, pepper, and olive oil.
Cut the chicken into pieces about 1½ inches across. Put them in the marinade and stir until every piece is coated.
Wash your hands, the knife, and the cutting board with hot, soapy water.
Cover the bowl and put it in the fridge.
steps.tip: You can marinate it in the morning and cook it at dinner.

steps.text: While it marinates, stir together the sauce's yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, and salt in the small bowl. Put it in the fridge.
Rinse the lettuce and tomatoes. Shred the lettuce, slice the tomatoes, and slice the pickles if you're using them.
Move an oven rack so the top of the sheet pan will sit about 6 inches below the broiler. Line the sheet pan with foil. Turn the broiler on high.
Thread the chicken onto the skewers, leaving a little space between pieces, and lay them on the pan. Pour the leftover marinade down the drain.
Wash your hands, and put the marinade bowl in the sink.
Put the pan under the broiler and broil until the tops are browned with a few dark spots.
steps.tip: Stay by the oven. A broiler can char food fast.

steps.text: Pull the pan out with oven mitts. Turn each skewer over with the tongs and broil the other side.
Slide the thermometer into the thickest piece of chicken. It needs to read at least 165°F. If it doesn't, broil 2 more minutes and check again.
Turn off the broiler. Wrap the pitas in a damp paper towel and microwave them until warm.
Slide the chicken off the skewers onto the plate with a fork. Spread garlic sauce on each pita, then add chicken, lettuce, tomato, and pickles, and roll it up.
steps.tip: Metal skewers stay hot for a long time. Hold them with an oven mitt.

marinade.text: Peel and mince the garlic, keeping the sauce's clove apart. In the large bowl, whisk the marinade's yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, and salt with the tomato paste, paprika, cumin, pepper, and olive oil.

cut.text: On the raw-meat board, unroll each thigh and trim off thick fat and gristle. Cut the thighs into 1½-inch cubes and add them to the marinade. Stir until every piece is coated. Don't rinse the chicken.
cut.look: Cubes close to the same size, with no thick fat left on them.

wash-cut.text: Wash your hands, the knife, and the board in the hot, soapy water, and wipe the counter.

chill.text: Cover the bowl and refrigerate it at least 30 minutes, or up to 8 hours.

sauce.text: Stir together the sauce's yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, and salt in the small bowl, and refrigerate it.

veg.text: Rinse the lettuce and tomatoes. Shred the lettuce into ¼-inch ribbons, slice the tomatoes into ¼-inch rounds, and slice the pickles if you're using them.

thread.text: Thread the cubes onto the skewers with a little space between them, and lay the skewers on the pan 1 inch apart. Pour the leftover marinade down the drain.

wash-thread.text: Wash your hands and put the marinade bowl in the hot, soapy water.

broil-1.text: Broil until the tops are browned with some charred edges.

turn.text: Pull out the pan with oven mitts, turn each skewer with the tongs, and broil the second side.

check.text: Check the thickest cube on three different skewers. Each needs at least 165°F. Return any that don't to the broiler for 2 minutes and check again.

serve.text: Slide the chicken off the skewers onto the clean plate with a fork. Spread garlic sauce on each pita, add chicken, lettuce, tomato, and pickles, and roll it up. Wash the thermometer probe.

add.text: Set up your raw-meat station as in this week's drill: a clean counter, the raw-meat board on a damp paper towel, a plate for cooked food, hot, soapy water ready, and the thermometer calibrated. If you're using wooden skewers, put them in water to soak.
add.tip: This is the mastery check. Work through it on your own; the adult watches but doesn't step in.

move.title: Raw to safe, on your own
move.body: This is the unit's mastery week. You'll set up your own raw-meat station, trim and cube chicken thighs, marinate them in yogurt, lemon, garlic, and spices, and broil them on skewers until charred at the edges and 165°F in the middle, with no one stepping in. Shish taouk is Lebanon's chicken on skewers, wrapped in pita with garlic sauce.

quiz.q: Why are the cubes cut about 1½ inches?
choices: Small enough to cook through before burning, big enough to stay juicy
So more fit on a skewer
quiz.explain: Even cubes finish together under strong heat.

quiz.q: Where does the chicken marinate, and for how long at least?
choices: In the fridge, at least 30 minutes
quiz.explain: Longer in the fridge gives more flavor; never on the counter.

quiz.q: What happens to the leftover marinade?
choices: It's brushed on at the end

quiz.q: How many pieces do you check with the thermometer?
choices: The thickest piece on two or three skewers
quiz.explain: Char shows the outside; the thermometer shows the middle.

add.title: 1½-inch cubes
add.body: Under a broiler, the outside cooks fast. Pieces much smaller than 1½ inches dry out before they char; much bigger, and the outside burns before the middle reaches 165°F. Even cubes from trimmed thighs all finish together.
